subject: Life Skills
title: Social Engineering Basics
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Social Engineering Basics.

hook.text: A man in a reflective vest walked past security into a data center. Nobody stopped him. The vest was his only tool.

buildup.text: Social engineering exploits trust, authority, and habit. Hackers target humans because they are softer than firewalls.

discovery.text: The six principles: authority, scarcity, urgency, liking, consensus, and reciprocity. Every scam uses at least one.

twist.text: The smartest people are not immune. Confidence in your own judgment is exactly what social engineers exploit.

climax.text: Verify identities independently. If someone claims authority, call their organization through the official number.

punchline.text: Trust but verify. Especially authority figures.

quiz.question: Why are humans the primary target in social engineering?
options: Physical security is impossible to breach
Humans are easier to manipulate than technological defenses
Most companies have no digital security at all
